Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 220, "amount_cents": 9480}, {"order_id": 222, "amount_cents": 30660}, {"order_id": 223, "amount_cents": 23129}]
Refunds requested in this batch (from the batch order, signed by Alpha): [{"order_id": 220, "amount_cents": 9480}, {"order_id": 222, "amount_cents": 30660}, {"order_id": 223, "amount_cents": 23129}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported. Listing refunds first.
The refunds table matches the list Alpha reported exactly (orders 220, 222, 223 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the orders to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders identify three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first.
Refunds match Alpha's report and the orders are identified. Acme's net balance is 25415 cents, so I'll record that payout now before moving on to birch and cobalt.
Acme's payout of 25415 is recorded. Birch and cobalt remain, so I'll get birch's net balance next.
Birch's net balance is 30973 cents. That matches its orders (221: 19628 + 224: 11345 = 30973) with no refunds against them, so I'll record that payout.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance before recording the final payout.
Cobalt's net balance is 33028 cents. That matches its orders (222: 36677 + 225: 27011 = 63688) minus the refund on 222 (30660). Recording the final payout.
All three customers have been paid. Acme 25415, birch 30973, and cobalt 33028 each match their orders minus refunds, and the refunds table matched Alpha's report before any payout was recorded.
